   431	   277	    // Foreign = a different stable session, OR any platform mismatch — the
   432	   278	    // platform is provable even when the events carry no session hint (audit
   433	   279	    // finding: a hint-less /baton:handoff narrative from claude-code silently
   434	   280	    // merged into — then sealed — a codex-owned bundle, corrupting the origin
   435	   281	    // the receive-side role avoidance keys on).
   436	   282	    const incomingLabel = stableIncoming ? stableIncoming.sessionHint : '(no session hint)';
   437	   283	    const foreign = stableIncoming
   438	   284	      ? stableIncoming.sessionHint !== originHint || platform !== active.origin.platform
   439	   285	      : platform !== active.origin.platform;
   440	   286	    if (foreign && flags['take-over'] !== true) {
   441	   287	      io.stderr.write(
   442	   288	        `baton checkpoint: event from a foreign session/origin (${platform}/${incomingLabel} vs active ${active.origin.platform}/${originHint}) — rejected to keep sessions isolated; rerun with --take-over to archive the active bundle and start fresh\n`,
   443	   289	      );
   444	   290	      return finish({ ok: false, error: { code: 'foreign-session', msg: 'event from a foreign session/origin rejected; rerun with --take-over' } }, 0);
   445	   291	    }
   446	   292	    if (foreign) {
   447	   293	      rotateJournal(root, 'takeover', io);
   448	   294	      const fresh = emptyBundle(
   449	   295	        { platform, model: typeof flags.model === 'string' ? flags.model : 'unknown', goal: active.task?.goal ?? 'unknown' },
   450	   296	        io.now(),
   451	   297	      );
   452	   298	      if (stableIncoming) fresh.origin.sessionHint = stableIncoming.sessionHint;
   453	   299	      writeSnapshot(root, fresh, io);
   454	   300	      io.stderr.write(`baton checkpoint: took over — prior bundle archived to history/, fresh bundle owned by ${platform}/${incomingLabel}\n`);
   455	   301	      active = fresh;
   456	   302	      mustRewrite = true;
   457	   303	    }
   458	   304	  }
   459	   305	
   460	   306	  if (unstableIncoming) {
   461	   307	    io.stderr.write('baton checkpoint: event carries an unstable (generated) session hint — ownership unverifiable; applied with this warning only\n');
   462	   308	  }
   463	   309	
   464	   310	  if (active === null) {
   465	   311	    active = emptyBundle(
   466	   312	      { platform, model: typeof flags.model === 'string' ? flags.model : 'unknown', goal: 'unknown' },
   467	   313	      io.now(),
   468	   314	    );
   469	   315	    writeSnapshot(root, active, io);
   470	   316	    // Self-applying seed event (gate-2 iter-2 B6): a journal-only rebuild
   471	   317	    // (snapshot + .bak both lost) must restore the bundle's identity, not the
   472	   318	    // "unknown" placeholder resolveBase seeds. bundle.seed carries bundleId,
   473	   319	    // origin, task, and generation and is applied on replay.
   474	   320	    appendJournal(
   475	   321	      root,
   476	   322	      {
   477	   323	        ts: io.now(),
   478	   324	        type: 'bundle.seed',
   479	   325	        payload: {
   480	   326	          bundleId: active.bundleId,
   481	   327	          generation: active.generation,
   482	   328	          createdAt: active.createdAt,
   483	   329	          origin: active.origin,
   484	   330	          task: { goal: active.task.goal },
   485	   331	          text: `[seed] auto-seeded a new bundle on ${platform} (model ${active.origin.model})`,
   486	   332	        },
   487	   333	        writerId: [platform, io.pid, 'seed'].join('-'),
   488	   334	        dedupeKey: dedupeKey({ ts: io.now(), type: 'bundle.seed', bundleId: active.bundleId }),
   489	   335	      },
   490	   336	      io,
   491	   337	    );
   492	   338	    io.stderr.write('baton checkpoint: no bundle found — auto-seeded a new one at .handoff/bundle.json\n');
   493	   339	    mustRewrite = true;
   494	   340	  }
   495	   341	
   496	   342	  // Ownership adoption (gate-2 fix 2): a bundle whose owner is unverified — a
   497	   343	  // fresh seed (null hint) or a receive that defaulted to an unstable hint —
   498	   344	  // adopts the first STABLE same-platform session as its owner, so semantic
   499	   345	  // isolation engages from then on instead of never.
   500	   346	  const ownerUnverified = active.origin.sessionHint === null || active.origin.unstable === true;
   501	   347	  if (ownerUnverified && stableIncoming && active.origin.platform === platform) {
   502	   348	    active = { ...active, origin: { ...active.origin, sessionHint: stableIncoming.sessionHint, unstable: false } };
   503	   349	    writeSnapshot(root, active, io);
   504	   350	    io.stderr.write(`baton checkpoint: adopted ${platform}/${stableIncoming.sessionHint} as the bundle owner (first verified session)\n`);
   505	   351	    mustRewrite = true;
   506	   352	  }
   507	   353	
   508	   354	  let lastSeq = 0;
   509	   355	  for (const ev of events) {
   510	   356	    const ts = typeof ev.ts === 'string' ? ev.ts : io.now();
   511	   357	    const entry = {
   512	   358	      ...ev,
   513	   359	      ts,
   514	   360	      dedupeKey:
   515	   361	        typeof ev.dedupeKey === 'string' && ev.dedupeKey.length > 0
   516	   362	          ? ev.dedupeKey
   517	   363	          : dedupeKey({ ts, type: ev.type, payload: ev.payload, source: ev.source, sessionHint: ev.sessionHint }),
   518	   364	      writerId: [platform, io.pid, ev.sessionHint ?? 'local'].join('-'),
   519	   365	    };
   520	   366	    lastSeq = appendJournal(root, entry, io);
   521	   367	  }
   522	   368	
   523	   369	  const snap = safeReadJson(io.fs, paths.snapshot);
   524	   370	  const snapSeq = snap.ok && typeof snap.value?.journalSeq === 'number' ? snap.value.journalSeq : 0;
   525	   371	  const snapUpdated = snap.ok && typeof snap.value?.updatedAt === 'string' ? Date.parse(snap.value.updatedAt) : 0;
   526	   372	  const important = events.some((/** @type {any} */ e) => !ROUTINE_TYPES.has(e.type));
   527	   373	  const elapsed = Date.parse(io.now()) - snapUpdated > THROTTLE_WINDOW_MS;
   528	   374	  const accreted = lastSeq - snapSeq;
   529	   375	
   530	   376	  let rewritten = false;
   531	   377	  if (mustRewrite || important || elapsed || accreted >= THROTTLE_EVENT_COUNT) {
   532	   378	    // Bounded git refresh on EVERY snapshot rewrite (gate-2 iter-2 M1): a
   533	   379	    // mechanical checkpoint carries branch/HEAD/dirty. Capture git BEFORE the
   534	   380	    // lock — it is async and must not straddle the lock — then do ONE atomic
   535	   381	    // read-modify-write UNDER the lock (iter-5 A1): reload the bundle inside the
   536	   382	    // lock, apply git, and write with the fencing token. The old code loaded
   537	   383	    // outside the lock, awaited git (yielding the event loop), then wrote the
   538	   384	    // stale bundle, so a concurrent --take-over during the await was clobbered
   539	   385	    // (origin rolled back, the new owner's event lost). Reloading inside the
   540	   386	    // lock guarantees the write is built from current state.
   541	   387	    const git = await gitSnapshot({ execFile: io.execFile, cwd: root, fs: io.fs });
   542	   388	    rewritten = withLock(root, io, (token) => {
   543	   389	      const merged = loadBundle(root, io).bundle;
   544	   390	      if (!merged) return false;
   545	   391	      if (git !== null) {
   546	   392	        merged.git = git;
   547	   393	      } else {
   548	   394	        // git refresh failed/timed out (iter-4 I2/F5): NEVER retain the prior
   549	   395	        // snapshot — stale HEAD/dirty presented as current corrupts the
   550	   396	        // receive-side evidence audit. Clear to explicit unavailable (null) and
   551	   397	        // warn; a repo that was never git (already null) warns nothing.
   552	   398	        if (merged.git !== null) {
   553	   399	          io.stderr.write('baton checkpoint: git refresh failed — clearing stale git state (marked unavailable; receive re-derives it live)\n');
   554	   400	        }
   555	   401	        merged.git = null;
   556	   402	      }
   557	   403	      writeSnapshotIn(root, merged, io, token);
   558	   404	      return true;
   559	   405	    });
   560	   406	  }
   561	   407	  return finish({ ok: true, data: { events: events.length, rewritten } }, 0);
   562	   408	}

   575	     9	// RED — `baton checkpoint --session <hint>` (subtask l1-checkpoint-session).
   576	    10	//
   577	    11	// Source of truth: docs/plans/2026-07-18-goal-loop-tasks.md subtask 2
   578	    12	//   (`checkpoint --session <hint>` flag: supervisor-owned stable session
   579	    13	//   identity) and docs/plans/2026-07-18-goal-loop-worktree-pipeline.md
   580	    14	//   §"Root + ownership discipline".
   581	    15	//
   582	    16	// The loop supervisor must checkpoint under its OWN stable session identity
   583	    17	// (`--session loop-<runId>`) regardless of what the piped hook payload carries,
   584	    18	// so its checkpoints land in ITS bundle and a concurrent child's payload
   585	    19	// session id can never masquerade as, or collide with, the supervisor owner.
   586	    20	//
   587	    21	// CONTRACT (pinned here):
   588	    22	//   S1. STRICT SPEC. `--session <hint>` is a KNOWN string flag: `--session abc`
   589	    23	//       parses and composes with the existing flags; a stray positional or an
   590	    24	//       unknown flag alongside it still exits 2 (unchanged strict parsing).
   591	    25	//   S2. NO SILENT FALLBACK. `--session ''` (empty value) is a usage error
   592	    26	//       (exit 2) whose message NAMES the flag and states it must be non-empty —
   593	    27	//       a supervisor bug that passes an empty hint must NOT silently fall back
   594	    28	//       to payload-derived identity. (Distinct from today's "unknown flag":
   595	    29	//       the message must mention "empty", never "unknown flag".)
   596	    30	//   S3. IDENTITY OVERRIDE. With `--session sup-1`, every checkpoint event's
   597	    31	//       effective session hint is `sup-1` (stable, unstable:false) — even when
   598	    32	//       the piped payload carries a DIFFERENT stable session_id. Asserted via
   599	    33	//       persisted state: origin.sessionHint and the journal writerId.
   600	    34	//   S4. OWNERSHIP SEMANTICS UNCHANGED, keyed on the effective (overridden) hint:
   601	    35	//       (a) seeding — first --session checkpoint into a fresh bundle records
   602	    36	//           that hint as the active owner;
   603	    37	//       (b) first-party — a second --session checkpoint with the same hint
   604	    38	//           lands (no foreign rejection);
   605	    39	//       (c) foreign — a --session X checkpoint into a bundle owned by stable
   606	    40	//           session Y is rejected exactly like today's foreign-stable case
   607	    41	//           (exit 0, --take-over named, memfs byte-identical); --take-over
   608	    42	//           still supersedes (fresh bundle owned by X);
   609	    43	//       (d) no --session — behaves exactly as today (regression negative).
   610	    44	//   S5. GUARD PRECEDENCE. BATON_SUPERVISED_CHILD set + --session → still the
   611	    45	//       silent no-op (the subtask-1 guard beats the flag).
   612	    46	//
   613	    47	// PROOF-OF-RED NOTE: `--session` is currently an UNKNOWN strict flag, so today
   614	    48	// cmdCheckpoint exits 2 ("unknown flag --session") before run(). The

   989	   168	export function writeSnapshotIn(root, bundle, io, token) {

  1003	   182	    }

  1005	   184	    atomicWriteText(io.fs, p.handoffMd, renderHandoffMd(bounded));
  1006	   185	  });

  1061	   240	 * Lock-context rotation: caller holds the lock and passes its fencing token.
  1062	   241	 * @param {string} root @param {'finalize'|'takeover'|'receive'} kind @param {any} io @param {string} token
  1063	   242	 * @returns {string} the history stem for this rotation
  1064	   243	 */
  1065	   244	export function rotateJournalIn(root, kind, io, token) {
  1066	   245	  const p = bundlePaths(root);
  1067	   246	  return guardedWrite(root, io, token, () => {
  1068	   247	    assertHandoffTreeSafe(root, io);
  1069	   248	    ensureDir(io.fs, p.dir);
  1070	   249	    const startedAt = io.now();

  1072	   251	    const snap = safeReadJson(io.fs, p.snapshot);
  1073	   252	    const seq = snap.ok && typeof snap.value?.journalSeq === 'number' ? snap.value.journalSeq : 0;
  1074	   253

  1076	   255	    ensureDir(io.fs, p.historyDir);

  1080	   259	      // never leave a partial history snapshot that recovery would trust.

  1084	   263	    }

  1087	   266	    } else {

  1089	   268	    }
  1090	   269	    atomicWriteText(io.fs, p.journal, '');
  1091	   270	
  1092	   271	    // Retention: newest RETAIN_PER_KIND per kind (ISO-derived stems sort by time).
  1093	   272	    const freezes = io.fs
  1094	   273	      .readdirSync(p.historyDir)
  1095	   274	      .filter((/** @type {string} */ n) => n.endsWith(`.${kind}.json`))
  1096	   275	      .sort();

  1103	   282	        } catch {

  1105	   284	        }
  1106	   285	      }
  1107	   286	    }
  1108	   287	
  1109	   288	    io.fs.unlinkSync(markerPath(p));

  1111	   290	  });

  1165	    47	    } catch {

  1207	    89	 * rejected the REAL platform's checkpoints as foreign.
  1208	    90	 * @param {string | boolean | undefined} value

  1210	    92	 */
  1211	    93	export function platformError(value) {

  1216	    98	
  1217	    99	/**
  1218	   100	 * Strict flag parser (surface-audit fold; docs/design/core.md §tooling always
  1219	   101	 * specified strict parsing). spec maps each flag name to 'string' | 'boolean';
  1220	   102	 * `json` and `root` are implied common flags. Errors — unknown flag, stray
  1221	   103	 * positional, missing string-flag value — return {error} so the command exits
  1222	   104	 * 2 instead of silently losing intent: the lenient parser let a stray token
  1223	   105	 * flip SAFETY flags off (checkpoint/doctor --strict, remap --native-only,
  1224	   106	 * receive --print-prompt all read fail-dangerous exit 0).
  1225	   107	 * @param {string[]} args
  1226	   108	 * @param {Record<string, 'string' | 'boolean'>} spec
  1227	   109	 * @returns {{flags: Record<string, string | boolean>, error?: string}}
  1228	   110	 */
  1229	   111	export function parseFlagsStrict(args, spec) {
  1230	   112	  /** @type {Record<string, 'string' | 'boolean'>} */
  1231	   113	  const full = { json: 'boolean', root: 'string', ...spec };
  1232	   114	  /** @type {Record<string, string | boolean>} */
  1233	   115	  const flags = {};
  1234	   116	  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i += 1) {
  1235	   117	    const a = args[i];
  1236	   118	    if (!a.startsWith('--')) return { flags, error: `unexpected argument '${a}' — flags are --name [value]` };
  1237	   119	    const key = a.slice(2);
  1238	   120	    const kind = full[key];
  1239	   121	    if (kind === undefined) return { flags, error: `unknown flag --${key}` };
  1240	   122	    if (kind === 'boolean') {
  1241	   123	      // A following token that is not a flag would have been this flag's
  1242	   124	      // silent "value" under the lenient parser; reject it loudly.
  1243	   125	      const next = args[i + 1];
  1244	   126	      if (next !== undefined && !next.startsWith('--')) {
  1245	   127	        return { flags, error: `unexpected token '${next}' after --${key} (a bare flag takes no value)` };
  1246	   128	      }
  1247	   129	      flags[key] = true;
  1248	   130	      continue;
  1249	   131	    }
  1250	   132	    const next = args[i + 1];
  1251	   133	    // A string flag consumes the next token unless it is itself a KNOWN flag
  1252	   134	    // (so `--commit --origin x` errors instead of eating '--origin').
  1253	   135	    if (next === undefined || (next.startsWith('--') && full[next.slice(2)] !== undefined)) {
  1254	   136	      return { flags, error: `--${key} requires a value` };
  1255	   137	    }
  1256	   138	    flags[key] = next;
  1257	   139	    i += 1;
  1258	   140	  }
  1259	   141	  return { flags };
  1260	   142	}
  1261	   143	
  1262	   144	/**
  1263	   145	 * Minimal flag parser: `--key value` pairs (value = next token not starting
  1264	   146	 * with --), bare `--key` booleans, positionals collected in order.
  1265	   147	 * @param {string[]} args
  1266	   148	 * @returns {{flags: Record<string, string | boolean>, positionals: string[]}}
  1267	   149	 */
  1268	   150	export function parseFlags(args) {
  1269	   151	  /** @type {Record<string, string | boolean>} */
  1270	   152	  const flags = {};
  1271	   153	  /** @type {string[]} */
  1272	   154	  const positionals = [];
  1273	   155	  for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i += 1) {
  1274	   156	    const a = args[i];
  1275	   157	    if (a.startsWith('--')) {
  1276	   158	      const key = a.slice(2);
  1277	   159	      const next = args[i + 1];
  1278	   160	      if (next !== undefined && !next.startsWith('--')) {
  1279	   161	        flags[key] = next;
  1280	   162	        i += 1;
  1281	   163	      } else {
  1282	   164	        flags[key] = true;
  1283	   165	      }
  1284	   166	    } else {
  1285	   167	      positionals.push(a);
  1286	   168	    }
  1287	   169	  }
  1288	   170	  return { flags, positionals };
  1289	   171	}

  2016	    31	## Design
  2017	    32	
  2018	    33	### Loop spec
  2019	    34	
  2020	    35	`loop.json` at repo root (schema `baton/loop@1`), scaffolded by
  2021	    36	`baton loop init "<goal>"`:
  2022	    37	
  2023	    38	- `goal`, `constraints[]` (falsifiable acceptance criteria — the loop's exit
  2024	    39	  condition), `smoke` ({cmd, expect} — the staged-gate slice definition),
  2025	    40	- `phases` — an ordered list of `{id, role}` entries: `id` is a free label
  2026	    41	  for progress display; `role` MUST be a matrix role ID (validation fails on
  2027	    42	  any unknown role before a child spawns). Default:
  2028	    43	  plan(`planner`) → gate-1(`plan-reviewer`) → smoke — itself a TDD mini-cycle
  2029	    44	  per the repo contract: smoke-tests(`test-author`) →
  2030	    45	  smoke-verify(`test-verifier`) → smoke-build(`implementer`) → the human
  2031	    46	  smoke gate — → per-subtask cycle (`test-author` → `test-verifier` →
  2032	    47	  `implementer` → `subtask-reviewer`) → gate-2(`final-reviewer-a`,
  2033	    48	  `final-reviewer-b`) → done,
  2034	    49	- `budgets` ({iterationCap: 5, perRoleTimeoutMin, maxChildrenPerPhase}),
  2035	    50	- roles resolve through the existing `baton.config.json` matrix — never
  2036	    51	  hardcoded models.
  2037	    52	
  2038	    53	### Role-matrix additions (Gate-1 iteration 1, finding 1)
  2039	    54	
  2040	    55	The loop references roles by ID only; every referenced role must exist in the
  2041	    56	matrix or `loop.json` validation fails (`unknown role '<id>'`, exit 2, before
  2042	    57	any child spawns). Four roles are ADDED to `baton.config.json` +
  2043	    58	`templates/baton.config.json.tpl` in the first implementation task:
  2044	    59	
  2045	    60	- `subtask-reviewer` — per-subtask diff review inside the loop cycle.
  2046	    61	- `merger` — the only role that writes main in pipeline mode; adversarial
  2047	    62	  re-check before merge.
  2048	    63	- `worker-a`, `worker-b` — the two pipeline seats. Subtask N assigns
  2049	    64	  writer = seat (N mod 2), reviewer = the other seat; the SEATS swap, and each
  2050	    65	  seat's concrete platform/model comes from its configured chain via the
  2051	    66	  resolver. No vendor or model name appears in this plan, child prompts, or
  2052	    67	  loop code — chains live in config only.
  2053	    68	
  2054	    69	### `baton loop` (Layer 2)
  2055	    70	
  2056	    71	- `baton loop init <goal>` — scaffold spec + plan template; idempotent,
  2057	    72	  dry-run-able, same two-phase plan/apply discipline as `baton init`.
  2058	    73	- `baton loop run [--approve-smoke <token>]` — the state machine. State lives
  2059	    74	  in gitignored `.handoff/loop/state.json` + `journal.ndjson` (same atomic
  2060	    75	  write + journal replay machinery as the bundle; loop position is also
  2061	    76	  checkpointed into the handoff bundle so a limit death carries it).
  2062	    77	
  2063	    78	### Root + ownership discipline (Gate-1 iteration 1, finding 2)
  2064	    79	
  2065	    80	One authoritative root: the MAIN repo root where `loop.json` lives. The
  2066	    81	supervisor is the SOLE writer of `.handoff/loop/` and of the main root's
  2067	    82	handoff bundle; every supervisor-driven baton invocation passes explicit
  2068	    83	`--root <mainRoot>` and a supervisor-owned stable session hint
  2069	    84	(`--session loop-<runId>` — a NEW flag added to `checkpoint`; `receive`
  2070	    85	already has it), so the bundle has exactly one stable owner.
  2071	    86	
  2072	    87	**Child-hook policy (Gate-1 iteration 2, finding 1; iteration 3,
  2073	    88	finding 1)** — children never touch OR read any bundle, by construction: the
  2074	    89	supervisor sets `BATON_SUPERVISED_CHILD=1` in every child's environment, and
  2075	    90	EVERY baton hook command — the hook entrypoints, `baton checkpoint`, and
  2076	    91	`baton session-start` (which would otherwise read the bundle and inject
  2077	    92	pending-handoff resume context into the child) — quietly no-ops (exit 0,
  2078	    93	empty output) when it is set. This covers
  2079	    94	Layer-2 children running in the MAIN root (where root discovery would
  2080	    95	otherwise find the supervisor-owned bundle and the foreign-session guard
  2081	    96	would reject their stable hints) and pipeline children in worktrees alike;
  2082	    97	narrative checkpointing for supervised work is the supervisor's job, driven
  2083	    98	by parsed child results. Contract tests: (a) Layer-2 — two concurrent
  2084	    99	main-root children with distinct stable session hints and live hooks →
  2085	   100	zero bundle mutations, zero foreign-session rejections, supervisor
  2086	   101	`--session` checkpoints land; (b) pipeline — same from two worktrees while
  2087	   102	the supervisor writes loop state.
  2088	   103	- Each role invocation is a headless child under the supervisor:
  2089	   104	  - claude-code roles: `claude -p "<role prompt>" --permission-mode
  2090	   105	    acceptEdits --allowedTools ...` (allowlist per role: reviewers read-only).
  2091	   106	  - codex roles: `codex exec -C <root> -s <sandbox> --model <m> -c
  2092	   107	    model_reasoning_effort=<e> "<prompt>" </dev/null` (stdin closed — the
  2093	   108	    stdin-hang class is a known field failure).
  2094	   109	  - Verdict contract: children end with the structured tail
  2095	   110	    (`VERDICT: APPROVED|APPROVED_WITH_NOTES|BLOCKED` + FINDINGS) already used
  2096	   111	    by every review gate; the supervisor parses exactly that.
  2097	   112	
  2098	   113	### Child supervision contract (Gate-1 iteration 1, finding 7)
  2099	   114	
  2100	   115	`children.mjs` owns the full child lifecycle, not just argv assembly:
  2101	   116	
  2102	   117	- Spawn detached in its OWN process group; stdin closed at spawn (the
  2103	   118	  codex-exec stdin-hang class); per-role timeout → SIGTERM to the group, 10 s
  2104	   119	  grace, then SIGKILL to the group (no zombie grandchildren; reap verified in
  2105	   120	  tests with a child that forks a sleeper).
  2106	   121	- Full child output streams to `.handoff/loop/children/<child-id>.log` with a
  2107	   122	  byte cap (head preserved, middle truncated with a marker — the verdict tail
  2108	   123	  is at the END so the tail is never truncated).
  2109	   124	- **Verdict parsing is region-bounded (prompt-echo defense)**: only the
  2110	   125	  child's FINAL message region is parsed — claude-code children run with a
  2111	   126	  structured output format and the parser reads the result field; codex
  2112	   127	  children are parsed strictly AFTER the last `tokens used` marker. The
  2113	   128	  prompt region (which quotes `VERDICT:` in its instructions) is never
  2114	   129	  scanned. Multiple tails in the final region → the LAST one wins.
  2115	   130	- An unparseable, absent, or truncated verdict is BLOCKED-with-escalation,
  2116	   131	  never APPROVED; a child that exits after making edits but before a verdict
  2117	   132	  parks the subtask with its worktree preserved for inspection.
  2118	   133	- A generic nonzero exit classifies as `other-error` (existing classifier
  2119	   134	  rule) → the loop retries once, then parks; it NEVER triggers limit failover
  2120	   135	  without limit-specific evidence.
  2121	   136	- Fixture-driven tests: prompt echo, multiple verdict tails, truncated
  2122	   137	  transcript, timeout kill/reap, zombie grandchild, non-limit nonzero exit.
  2123	   138	
  2124	   139	### Supervisor lifetime and recovery (Gate-1 iteration 2, finding 5)
  2125	   140	
  2126	   141	"Survives the operator's session ending" is a defined mechanism, not a hope:
  2127	   142	
  2128	   143	- `baton loop run` is FOREGROUND by default. `--detach` re-launches the
  2129	   144	  supervisor in its own session (`setsid`), output to
  2130	   145	  `.handoff/loop/supervisor.log`, and returns.
  2131	   146	- A run lock `.handoff/loop/supervisor.lock` carries {pid, process
  2132	   147	  start-time, host, runId} — the same provably-dead machinery as the
  2133	   148	  Layer-1 bundle lock. A second `loop run` against a LIVE supervisor is
  2134	   149	  refused; against a provably-dead one it recovers.
  2135	   150	- The state machine is journal-replayable: recovery replays
  2136	   151	  `journal.ndjson`, marks any in-flight child of the dead supervisor as
  2137	   152	  interrupted (its process group is gone or killed on adoption), and either
  2138	   153	  continues from the last completed step or parks with an escalation note —
  2139	   154	  never re-runs a completed gate iteration.
  2140	   155	- Acceptance adds a supervisor-death test: kill the supervisor (and its
  2141	   156	  launching session) mid-subtask → a fresh `loop run` recovers via the
  2142	   157	  journal and continues or parks; no orphaned children survive (process
  2143	   158	  groups reaped on adoption).
  2144	   159	
  2145	   160	- **Smoke gate (staleness-proof — Gate-1 iteration 1, finding 8; TDD order —
  2146	   161	  iteration 2, finding 2)**: after gate-1, the smoke slice is built as a TDD
  2147	   162	  mini-cycle (test-author writes the failing smoke assertion → test-verifier
  2148	   163	  approves it → implementer writes only enough to pass it — the repo TDD
  2149	   164	  contract applies to the slice, not just to subtasks); the supervisor then
  2150	   165	  runs `smoke.cmd`, records output, and STOPS, writing
  2151	   166	  `.handoff/loop/SMOKE-REVIEW.md` plus `smoke-approval.json` containing an
  2152	   167	  approval token = digest over {loop-state digest, smoke.cmd, output digest,
  2153	   168	  HEAD, content-sensitive git digest (existing snapshot machinery), child
  2154	   169	  assignment}. Resuming requires `baton loop run --approve-smoke <token>`;
  2155	   170	  the supervisor recomputes the digest first and REFUSES a drifted token
  2156	   171	  (anything changed since the human looked) — it parks for a fresh smoke run
  2157	   172	  instead. No full-run budget is spent before a valid approval.
  2158	   173	- **Limit failover (the baton integration — Gate-1 iteration 1, finding 3)**:
  2159	   174	  an exact transaction, not a loose chain. On child death: (1) reap the
  2160	   175	  process group and freeze the transcript; (2) classify via `baton detect`;
  2161	   176	  non-limit → the retry/park path above. On a limit classification:
  2162	   177	  (3) checkpoint the loop position INTO THE BUNDLE (supervisor
  2163	   178	  `checkpoint --session loop-<runId>`) so the seal carries it and the receipt
  2164	   179	  token binds it; (4) seal via `finalize --reason-class usage-limit --root
  2165	   180	  <mainRoot>` (an already-dead/unsealed bundle takes the degraded-open path
  2166	   181	  receive already supports); (5) refresh probes; (6) `receive --prepare` then
  2167	   182	  `--commit` back-to-back with IDENTICAL intake flags, the supervisor session
  2168	   183	  hint, and the same explicit root, with NO intervening writes; (7) resolver
  2169	   184	  output (with the dead entry avoided) picks the relaunch platform+model;
  2170	   185	  (8) relaunch the child with the resume prompt. A stale-token rejection
  2171	   186	  triggers ONE automatic re-prepare/commit retry; a second failure parks.
  2172	   187	  Between prepare and commit the failover holds the loop transaction lock and
  2173	   188	  writes NOTHING — `.handoff/loop/` writes are not token-bound inputs, so
  2174	   189	  this is enforced by construction and ASSERTED in tests (fs spy: zero
  2175	   190	  `.handoff/loop/` writes inside the window), not assumed. Drift-rejection
  2176	   191	  tests inject the inputs the token actually binds: git change and probe
  2177	   192	  refresh between prepare and commit → stale-token → one retry path. Plus:
  2178	   193	  open-bundle (unsealed) limit death; the full seal→receive→relaunch happy
  2179	   194	  path.
  2180	   195	- **Model-level failover (Gate-1 iteration 1, finding 4)**: the resolver
  2181	   196	  gains entry-level avoidance — `avoidEntries: [{platform, model}]` alongside
  2182	   197	  the existing platform-level `avoid[]` — and the classifier gains a
  2183	   198	  `model-unavailable` signature class (distinct from usage-limit; seeded with
  2184	   199	  the verified account-tier rejection string). A model rejected at spawn adds
  2185	   200	  its {platform, model} entry to avoidEntries and re-resolves: other models
  2186	   201	  on the SAME platform remain selectable. Named test: first chain entry
  2187	   202	  rejected as model-unavailable → the next entry on the same platform is
  2188	   203	  selected, with no platform-wide avoidance.
  2189	   204	  All platforms/entries exhausted → the loop parks with a resume-at hint
  2190	   205	  instead of dying.
  2191	   206	- **Caps**: every gate loops at most 5 iterations; on exhaustion the loop
  2192	   207	  parks and escalates (writes `.handoff/loop/ESCALATION.md`, notifies) — never
  2193	   208	  a 6th run.
  2194	   209	
  2195	   210	### `baton pipeline` (Layer 3 — a loop preset)
  2196	   211	
  2197	   212	- `baton pipeline run` = `loop run` with the dual-worktree subtask cycle:
  2198	   213	  - Two persistent worktrees `.worktrees/wt-a`, `.worktrees/wt-b`
  2199	   214	    (`git worktree add`); `pipeline init` ensure-lines `.worktrees/` into
  2200	   215	    `.gitignore` (same idempotent machinery as the `.handoff/` line).
  2201	   216	  - Subtask N: the writer seat implements on a namespaced branch
  2202	   217	    (`baton/wt-<seat>/subtask-N`) in its worktree; the reviewer seat reviews
  2203	   218	    the diff from the OTHER worktree (fresh checkout, fresh context). Seats
  2204	   219	    swap every subtask: worker-a writes / worker-b reviews → worker-b writes /
  2205	   220	    worker-a reviews → … (concrete models per seat come from the role
  2206	   221	    matrix — see Role-matrix additions).
  2207	   222	  - Verdict flow: APPROVED → the merger role adversarially re-checks and
  2208	   223	    merges into main (the ONLY writer to main); BLOCKED → writer fixes,
  2209	   224	    ≤5 iterations, then escalate. After each merge both worktrees
  2210	   225	    fast-forward.
  2211	   226	
  2212	   227	  **Worktree transaction layer (Gate-1 iteration 1, finding 5)** —
  2213	   228	  `worktrees.mjs` treats every git operation as a guarded transaction:
  2214	   229	  - Branch namespace `baton/wt-*/…` is loop-owned; anything else is never
  2215	   230	    touched.
  2216	   231	  - Preflight before each child: worktree exists in `git worktree list`,
  2217	   232	    index clean, HEAD on the expected branch — a dirty or drifted worktree
  2218	   233	    parks the subtask instead of spawning.
  2219	   234	  - Postflight after each child: HEAD still on the expected branch, main
  2220	   235	    unmoved by the child — violation parks with the evidence.
  2221	   236	  - Merges run under a supervisor-held merge lock; worktree sync after merge
  2222	   237	    is ff-only (a non-ff sync is a corruption signal → park); merge conflicts
  2223	   238	    park + escalate, never auto-resolved.
  2224	   239	  - Stale metadata self-heals: a raw-deleted worktree directory is detected
  2225	   240	    (`git worktree list` vs fs), pruned (`git worktree prune`), and re-added;
  2226	   241	    teardown uses `git worktree remove` + branch deletion so acceptance
  2227	   242	    constraint 5 (no residue) holds.
  2228	   243	  - Adversarial tests: stale branch from a previous run, dirty worker,
  2229	   244	    main moved mid-subtask, merge conflict, raw-deleted `.worktrees/`,
  2230	   245	    untracked `.worktrees/` (missing gitignore line → doctor check).
  2231	   246	
  2232	   247	  **Attribution enforcement for child commits (Gate-1 iteration 1,
  2233	   248	  finding 6)** — the invariant is enforced, not assumed:
  2234	   249	  - The supervisor sets `GIT_AUTHOR_NAME/EMAIL` and `GIT_COMMITTER_NAME/EMAIL`
  2235	   250	    (sole author identity) in EVERY child's environment.
  2236	   251	  - Every merge is gated on an attribution scan over the exact range
  2237	   252	    `main..baton/wt-<seat>/subtask-N` — author/committer identity plus the
  2238	   253	    forbidden-trailer patterns (the existing doctor patterns, applied to the
  2239	   254	    full range, not a last-50 window). A violation blocks the merge and
  2240	   255	    parks.
  2241	   256	  - The existing doctor 50-commit scan remains the repo-wide backstop.
  2242	   257	
  2243	   258	### Module layout (all under `core/src/loop/`)
  2244	   259	
  2245	   260	`spec.mjs` (load/validate loop.json incl. role-existence check) · `state.mjs`
  2246	   261	(state machine + journal + smoke-approval token) · `children.mjs` (full child
  2247	   262	lifecycle: spawn/process-group/timeout/log-cap, region-bounded verdict parse,
  2248	   263	detect-on-exit) · `failover.mjs` (the limit-death transaction) ·
  2249	   264	`worktrees.mjs` (guarded git transactions, branch discipline, attribution
  2250	   265	range scan) · `commands/loop.mjs`, `commands/pipeline.mjs`. Plus three Layer-1
  2251	   266	extensions: `roles/resolve.mjs` gains `avoidEntries[]` (entry-level
  2252	   267	avoidance, backward-compatible — omitted means current behavior); the
  2253	   268	signature table gains the `model-unavailable` class; `checkpoint` gains a
  2254	   269	`--session <hint>` flag (supervisor identity), and the
  2255	   270	`BATON_SUPERVISED_CHILD` no-op guard lands in the hook entrypoints,
  2256	   271	`checkpoint`, AND `session-start` (every hook-invoked command).
  2257	   272	
  2258	   273	### Acceptance constraints (the loop's exit condition)
  2259	   274	
  2260	   275	1. On a fixture repo, `baton loop run` drives a toy goal end-to-end headlessly:
  2261	   276	   plan → gate-1 → smoke slice AS A TDD MINI-CYCLE (failing smoke assertion
  2262	   277	   authored and verifier-approved BEFORE the slice implementation — order
  2263	   278	   asserted from the journal) → parked for approval → (approved) → 2 subtasks
  2264	   279	   TDD → gate-2 → done, with review artifacts under `reviews/` in the fixture.
  2265	   280	   Layer-2 children run in the main root with live hooks and neither mutate
  2266	   281	   NOR read the supervisor-owned bundle: under `BATON_SUPERVISED_CHILD=1`,
  2267	   282	   hook commands on all three platforms produce zero bundle writes AND zero
  2268	   283	   session-start resume context (both asserted).
  2269	   284	2. Simulated limit death (child exits with a verbatim limit banner) mid-subtask
  2270	   285	   → the loop seals, remaps the role off the dead platform, resumes on the
  2271	   286	   other harness, and completes the subtask. Chained A→B→A tested. Separately:
  2272	   287	   a model-unavailable rejection at spawn selects the NEXT entry on the same
  2273	   288	   platform (no platform-wide avoidance).
  2274	   289	3. `baton pipeline run` completes 2 subtasks with alternating writer/reviewer
  2275	   290	   across the two worktrees; the attribution range scan passes for main AND
  2276	   291	   both worker branch ranges (child commits included) — sole author, zero AI
  2277	   292	   attribution; reviewer children run read-only.
  2278	   293	4. The 5-cap parks + escalates on every gate (unit-forced exhaustion test);
  2279	   294	   no gate ever runs a 6th iteration. Killing the supervisor (and its
  2280	   295	   launching session) mid-subtask → a fresh `loop run` recovers via the
  2281	   296	   journal and continues or parks, with no orphaned children.
  2282	   297	5. Deleting `.handoff/` and `.worktrees/` leaves the fixture repo exactly as
  2283	   298	   a plain git repo (no residue outside gitignored trees).
  2284	   299	6. All existing 878 tests stay green; the new suite covers spec validation,
  2285	   300	   state-machine transitions (unit, injected io), child verdict parsing
  2286	   301	   (fixture transcripts), failover (fake children), and worktree discipline.
  2287	   302	
  2288	   303	### Top risks
  2289	   304	
  2290	   305	1. **Headless permission surfaces** — Claude Code children need permission
  2291	   306	   flags that stay inside the sandboxed repo; reviewers get read-only
  2292	   307	   allowlists. Mitigation: per-role allowlist table + spike task 0.
  2293	   308	2. **Verdict-parse drift** — models sometimes wrap the tail; the
  2294	   309	   region-bounded parser (Child supervision contract) takes the LAST tail in
  2295	   310	   the final-message region only and treats an unparseable one as
  2296	   311	   BLOCKED-with-escalation, never as APPROVED.
  2297	   312	3. **Cost runaway** — per-phase child caps + iteration caps + the smoke gate
  2298	   313	   before any full-run spend; every child's token/duration logged to the loop
  2299	   314	   journal.
  2300	   315	4. **Worktree state divergence** — only the merger writes main; workers are
  2301	   316	   branch-jailed; ff-sync after each merge; `baton pipeline doctor` checks
  2302	   317	   worktree health.
  2303	   318	5. **Cross-platform child API drift** — the spawn contract lives in ONE module
  2304	   319	   (children.mjs) with per-platform fixtures, same seam discipline as
  2305	   320	   normalize.mjs.
  2306	   321	
  2307	   322	## Out of scope for this milestone
  2308	   323	
  2309	   324	Multi-repo loops; parallel subtask fan-out (>1 writer at once); cloud/cron
  2310	   325	driving (the supervisor is local-first; scheduled runs are a later layer);
  2311	   326	LLM-judged smoke verdicts (the smoke gate is a human gate by decision 3).
  2312	   327

  4537	     9	 * performs the atomic transition. The receiving session hint defaults to a
  4538	    10	 * host-stable value so prepare and commit issued by separate CLI processes
  4539	    11	 * still derive the same token; adapters pass `--session` with their real id.
  4540	    12	 * @param {string[]} args @param {any} io

  4542	    14	 */

  4796	    40	export function makeMemfs(initialFiles = {}) {
  4797	    41	  const store = new Map(); // path -> string content
  4798	    42	  const dirs = new Set(['/']);
  4799	    43	  const mtimes = new Map();
  4800	    44	  const history = [];
  4801	    45	  let clock = 0;
  4802	    46

  4816	    60	    const parent = dirname(np);

  4956	   200	        const size = Buffer.byteLength(store.get(np));
  4957	   201	        return { isFile: () => true, isDirectory: () => false, isSymbolicLink: () => false, size, mtimeMs: mtimes.get(np) || 0 };
  4958	   202	      }
  4959	   203	      if (dirs.has(np)) {
  4960	   204	        return { isFile: () => false, isDirectory: () => true, isSymbolicLink: () => false, size: 0, mtimeMs: mtimes.get(np) || 0 };
  4961	   205	      }
  4962	   206	      throw fsError('ENOENT', 'stat', np);
  4963	   207	    },
  4964	   208	
  4965	   209	    // The fake cannot represent symlinks, so lstat === stat and realpath is
  4966	   210	    // normalization. Symlink-refusal behavior is proven over the real fs in
  4967	   211	    // tests/integration/symlink-escape.test.mjs.
  4968	   212	    lstatSync(p) {
  4969	   213	      return fs.statSync(p);
  4970	   214	    },
  4971	   215	
  4972	   216	    realpathSync(p) {

  4974	   218	      if (!store.has(np) && !dirs.has(np)) throw fsError('ENOENT', 'realpath', np);
  4975	   219	      return np;
  4976	   220	    },
  4977	   221	
  4978	   222	    copyFileSync(src, dest) {
  4979	   223	      const ns = normalize(src);
  4980	   224	      const nd = normalize(dest);
  4981	   225	      if (!store.has(ns)) throw fsError('ENOENT', 'copyfile', ns);
  4982	   226	      ensureParent(nd, 'copyfile');

  4984	   228	      touch(nd);
  4985	   229	      record('copyFileSync', [ns, nd]);
  4986	   230	    },
  4987	   231	  };

  4998	     1	import { createHash } from 'node:crypto';
  4999	     2	
  5000	     3	// Git facts degrade to null rather than block a checkpoint: not-a-repo,
  5001	     4	// missing binary, and timeouts are all expected environments (plan §Root
  5002	     5	// discovery & degraded modes).
  5003	     6	const GIT_TIMEOUT_MS = 5000;
  5004	     7	// The untracked digest is bounded: beyond this many paths, entries fold in by
  5005	     8	// name only, keeping prepare-time hashing cheap on huge untracked trees.
  5006	     9	const UNTRACKED_CAP = 200;
  5007	    10	// NUL separator: cannot occur in diffs, sizes, hex hashes, or file paths, so
  5008	    11	// joined digest inputs cannot collide across field boundaries.
  5009	    12	const SEP = String.fromCharCode(0);
  5010	    13	const NEWLINE = String.fromCharCode(10);
  5011	    14	
  5012	    15	const sha256 = (/** @type {string} */ s) => createHash('sha256').update(s).digest('hex');
  5013	    16	
  5014	    17	/**
  5015	    18	 * Capture the repo's git state plus a content-sensitive digest. The digest
  5016	    19	 * covers the staged diff, unstaged diff, and a bounded untracked-files digest
  5017	    20	 * (path + size + content hash) — NOT the HEAD sha, which the receive token
  5018	    21	 * binds as its own input, so a HEAD-only move is distinguishable from a
  5019	    22	 * content change.
  5020	    23	 * @param {{execFile: Function, cwd: string, fs: any}} deps
  5021	    24	 * @returns {Promise<{branch: string, headSha: string, dirty: boolean, dirtySummary: string[], contentDigest: string} | null>}
  5022	    25	 */
  5023	    26	export async function snapshot({ execFile, cwd, fs }) {
  5024	    27	  const git = (/** @type {string[]} */ args) => execFile('git', args, { cwd, timeout: GIT_TIMEOUT_MS });
  5025	    28	  let branch, head, status, staged, unstaged, untrackedList;
  5026	    29	  try {
  5027	    30	    [branch, head, status, staged, unstaged, untrackedList] = await Promise.all([
  5028	    31	      git(['rev-parse', '--abbrev-ref', 'HEAD']),
  5029	    32	      git(['rev-parse', 'HEAD']),
  5030	    33	      git(['status', '--porcelain']),
  5031	    34	      git(['diff', '--cached']),
  5032	    35	      git(['diff']),
  5033	    36	      git(['ls-files', '--others', '--exclude-standard']),
  5034	    37	    ]);
  5035	    38	  } catch {
  5036	    39	    return null;
  5037	    40	  }
  5038	    41	
  5039	    42	  const nonEmptyLines = (/** @type {string} */ s) => s.split(NEWLINE).filter((/** @type {string} */ l) => l !== '');
  5040	    43	  const dirtySummary = nonEmptyLines(status.stdout);
  5041	    44	  const untrackedPaths = nonEmptyLines(untrackedList.stdout);
  5042	    45	
  5043	    46	  const untrackedEntries = untrackedPaths.map((rel, i) => {
  5044	    47	    if (i >= UNTRACKED_CAP) return [rel, 'capped'].join(SEP);
  5045	    48	    try {
  5046	    49	      const content = fs.readFileSync(cwd + '/' + rel, 'utf8');
  5047	    50	      return [rel, String(Buffer.byteLength(content)), sha256(content)].join(SEP);
  5048	    51	    } catch {
  5049	    52	      // Listed but unreadable (deleted mid-flight): still digest its presence.
  5050	    53	      return [rel, 'absent'].join(SEP);
  5051	    54	    }
  5052	    55	  });
  5053	    56	
  5054	    57	  return {
  5055	    58	    branch: branch.stdout.trim(),
  5056	    59	    headSha: head.stdout.trim(),
  5057	    60	    dirty: dirtySummary.length > 0,
  5058	    61	    dirtySummary,
  5059	    62	    contentDigest: sha256([staged.stdout, unstaged.stdout, ...untrackedEntries].join(SEP)),
  5060	    63	  };
  5061	    64	}

   350	    io.stderr.write(`baton checkpoint: adopted ${platform}/${stableIncoming.sessionHint} as the bundle owner (first verified session)\n`);
   351	    mustRewrite = true;
   352	  }
   353	
   354	  let lastSeq = 0;
   355	  for (const ev of events) {
   356	    const ts = typeof ev.ts === 'string' ? ev.ts : io.now();
   357	    const entry = {
   358	      ...ev,
   359	      ts,
   360	      dedupeKey:
   361	        typeof ev.dedupeKey === 'string' && ev.dedupeKey.length > 0
   362	          ? ev.dedupeKey
   363	          : dedupeKey({ ts, type: ev.type, payload: ev.payload, source: ev.source, sessionHint: ev.sessionHint }),
   364	      writerId: [platform, io.pid, ev.sessionHint ?? 'local'].join('-'),
   365	    };
   366	    lastSeq = appendJournal(root, entry, io);
   367	  }
   368	
   369	  const snap = safeReadJson(io.fs, paths.snapshot);
   370	  const snapSeq = snap.ok && typeof snap.value?.journalSeq === 'number' ? snap.value.journalSeq : 0;
   371	  const snapUpdated = snap.ok && typeof snap.value?.updatedAt === 'string' ? Date.parse(snap.value.updatedAt) : 0;
   372	  const important = events.some((/** @type {any} */ e) => !ROUTINE_TYPES.has(e.type));
   373	  const elapsed = Date.parse(io.now()) - snapUpdated > THROTTLE_WINDOW_MS;
   374	  const accreted = lastSeq - snapSeq;

   376	  let rewritten = false;
   377	  if (mustRewrite || important || elapsed || accreted >= THROTTLE_EVENT_COUNT) {
   378	    // Bounded git refresh on EVERY snapshot rewrite (gate-2 iter-2 M1): a
   379	    // mechanical checkpoint carries branch/HEAD/dirty. Capture git BEFORE the
   380	    // lock — it is async and must not straddle the lock — then do ONE atomic
   381	    // read-modify-write UNDER the lock (iter-5 A1): reload the bundle inside the
   382	    // lock, apply git, and write with the fencing token. The old code loaded
   383	    // outside the lock, awaited git (yielding the event loop), then wrote the
   384	    // stale bundle, so a concurrent --take-over during the await was clobbered
   385	    // (origin rolled back, the new owner's event lost). Reloading inside the
   386	    // lock guarantees the write is built from current state.
   387	    const git = await gitSnapshot({ execFile: io.execFile, cwd: root, fs: io.fs });
   388	    rewritten = withLock(root, io, (token) => {
   389	      const merged = loadBundle(root, io).bundle;
   390	      if (!merged) return false;
   391	      if (git !== null) {
   392	        merged.git = git;
   393	      } else {
   394	        // git refresh failed/timed out (iter-4 I2/F5): NEVER retain the prior
   395	        // snapshot — stale HEAD/dirty presented as current corrupts the
   396	        // receive-side evidence audit. Clear to explicit unavailable (null) and
   397	        // warn; a repo that was never git (already null) warns nothing.
   398	        if (merged.git !== null) {
   399	          io.stderr.write('baton checkpoint: git refresh failed — clearing stale git state (marked unavailable; receive re-derives it live)\n');
   400	        }
   401	        merged.git = null;
   402	      }
   403	      writeSnapshotIn(root, merged, io, token);
   404	      return true;
   405	    });
   406	  }
   407	  return finish({ ok: true, data: { events: events.length, rewritten } }, 0);
   408	}

   200	 * @param {string} root @param {any} entry @param {any} io

   203	export function appendJournal(root, entry, io) {

   205	  return withLock(root, io, (token) =>

   229	/**
   230	 * Crash-safe journal rotation (marker → freeze → rename → fresh journal →
   231	 * clear marker), with 10-per-kind history retention. Mutation — lock-gated.
   232	 * @param {string} root @param {'finalize'|'takeover'|'receive'} kind @param {any} io
   233	 * @returns {string} the history stem for this rotation
   234	 */
   235	export function rotateJournal(root, kind, io) {
   236	  return withLock(root, io, (token) => rotateJournalIn(root, kind, io, token));
   237	}
   238	
   239	/**
   240	 * Lock-context rotation: caller holds the lock and passes its fencing token.
   241	 * @param {string} root @param {'finalize'|'takeover'|'receive'} kind @param {any} io @param {string} token
   242	 * @returns {string} the history stem for this rotation
   243	 */
   244	export function rotateJournalIn(root, kind, io, token) {
   245	  const p = bundlePaths(root);
   246	  return guardedWrite(root, io, token, () => {
   247	    assertHandoffTreeSafe(root, io);
   248	    ensureDir(io.fs, p.dir);
   249	    const startedAt = io.now();
   250	    const stem = `${tsForFile(startedAt)}.${kind}`;
   251	    const snap = safeReadJson(io.fs, p.snapshot);
   252	    const seq = snap.ok && typeof snap.value?.journalSeq === 'number' ? snap.value.journalSeq : 0;
   253	
   254	    atomicWriteJson(io.fs, markerPath(p), { kind, startedAt, seq });
   255	    ensureDir(io.fs, p.historyDir);
   256	
   257	    if (io.fs.existsSync(p.snapshot)) {
   258	      // Atomic freeze (gate-2 minor 16): tmp+rename, so a crash mid-copy can
   259	      // never leave a partial history snapshot that recovery would trust.
   260	      atomicWriteText(io.fs, `${p.historyDir}/${stem}.json`, io.fs.readFileSync(p.snapshot, 'utf8'));
   261	    } else {
   262	      atomicWriteText(io.fs, `${p.historyDir}/${stem}.json`, '');
   263	    }
   264	    if (io.fs.existsSync(p.journal)) {
   265	      io.fs.renameSync(p.journal, `${p.historyDir}/${stem}.ndjson`);
   266	    } else {
   267	      atomicWriteText(io.fs, `${p.historyDir}/${stem}.ndjson`, '');
   268	    }
   269	    atomicWriteText(io.fs, p.journal, '');
   270	
   271	    // Retention: newest RETAIN_PER_KIND per kind (ISO-derived stems sort by time).
   272	    const freezes = io.fs
   273	      .readdirSync(p.historyDir)
   274	      .filter((/** @type {string} */ n) => n.endsWith(`.${kind}.json`))
   275	      .sort();

    21	   every subtask; the planner role plans and the merger role performs the
    22	   final adversarial merge (concrete chains live in `baton.config.json`).
    23	3. **Layer 2 smoke gate**: one staged gate after planning — the loop must
    24	   produce a minimal end-to-end slice (build + run + one real assertion) and
    25	   get explicit approval before the full run; the 5-iteration cap governs
    26	   every gate.
    27	4. **Driver**: a supervisor CLI — spawns headless role children
    28	   (`claude -p` / `codex exec`), parses verdicts, and invokes baton handoff
    29	   automatically on limit death. Survives the operator's session ending.
    30	
    31	## Design
    32	
    33	### Loop spec
    34	
    35	`loop.json` at repo root (schema `baton/loop@1`), scaffolded by
    36	`baton loop init "<goal>"`:
    37	
    38	- `goal`, `constraints[]` (falsifiable acceptance criteria — the loop's exit
    39	  condition), `smoke` ({cmd, expect} — the staged-gate slice definition),
    40	- `phases` — an ordered list of `{id, role}` entries: `id` is a free label
    41	  for progress display; `role` MUST be a matrix role ID (validation fails on
    42	  any unknown role before a child spawns). Default:
    43	  plan(`planner`) → gate-1(`plan-reviewer`) → smoke — itself a TDD mini-cycle
    44	  per the repo contract: smoke-tests(`test-author`) →
    45	  smoke-verify(`test-verifier`) → smoke-build(`implementer`) → the human
    46	  smoke gate — → per-subtask cycle (`test-author` → `test-verifier` →
    47	  `implementer` → `subtask-reviewer`) → gate-2(`final-reviewer-a`,
    48	  `final-reviewer-b`) → done,
    49	- `budgets` ({iterationCap: 5, perRoleTimeoutMin, maxChildrenPerPhase}),
    50	- roles resolve through the existing `baton.config.json` matrix — never
    51	  hardcoded models.
    52	
    53	### Role-matrix additions (Gate-1 iteration 1, finding 1)
    54	
    55	The loop references roles by ID only; every referenced role must exist in the
    56	matrix or `loop.json` validation fails (`unknown role '<id>'`, exit 2, before
    57	any child spawns). Four roles are ADDED to `baton.config.json` +
    58	`templates/baton.config.json.tpl` in the first implementation task:
    59	
    60	- `subtask-reviewer` — per-subtask diff review inside the loop cycle.
    61	- `merger` — the only role that writes main in pipeline mode; adversarial
    62	  re-check before merge.
    63	- `worker-a`, `worker-b` — the two pipeline seats. Subtask N assigns
    64	  writer = seat (N mod 2), reviewer = the other seat; the SEATS swap, and each
    65	  seat's concrete platform/model comes from its configured chain via the
    66	  resolver. No vendor or model name appears in this plan, child prompts, or
    67	  loop code — chains live in config only.
    68	
    69	### `baton loop` (Layer 2)
    70	
    71	- `baton loop init <goal>` — scaffold spec + plan template; idempotent,
    72	  dry-run-able, same two-phase plan/apply discipline as `baton init`.
    73	- `baton loop run [--approve-smoke <token>]` — the state machine. State lives
    74	  in gitignored `.handoff/loop/state.json` + `journal.ndjson` (same atomic
    75	  write + journal replay machinery as the bundle; loop position is also
    76	  checkpointed into the handoff bundle so a limit death carries it).
    77	
    78	### Root + ownership discipline (Gate-1 iteration 1, finding 2)
    79	
    80	One authoritative root: the MAIN repo root where `loop.json` lives. The
    81	supervisor is the SOLE writer of `.handoff/loop/` and of the main root's
    82	handoff bundle; every supervisor-driven baton invocation passes explicit
    83	`--root <mainRoot>` and a supervisor-owned stable session hint
    84	(`--session loop-<runId>` — a NEW flag added to `checkpoint`; `receive`
    85	already has it), so the bundle has exactly one stable owner.
    86	
    87	**Child-hook policy (Gate-1 iteration 2, finding 1; iteration 3,
    88	finding 1)** — children never touch OR read any bundle, by construction: the
    89	supervisor sets `BATON_SUPERVISED_CHILD=1` in every child's environment, and
    90	EVERY baton hook command — the hook entrypoints, `baton checkpoint`, and
    91	`baton session-start` (which would otherwise read the bundle and inject
    92	pending-handoff resume context into the child) — quietly no-ops (exit 0,
    93	empty output) when it is set. This covers
    94	Layer-2 children running in the MAIN root (where root discovery would
    95	otherwise find the supervisor-owned bundle and the foreign-session guard
    96	would reject their stable hints) and pipeline children in worktrees alike;
    97	narrative checkpointing for supervised work is the supervisor's job, driven
    98	by parsed child results. Contract tests: (a) Layer-2 — two concurrent
    99	main-root children with distinct stable session hints and live hooks →
   100	zero bundle mutations, zero foreign-session rejections, supervisor
   101	`--session` checkpoints land; (b) pipeline — same from two worktrees while
   102	the supervisor writes loop state.
   103	- Each role invocation is a headless child under the supervisor:
   104	  - claude-code roles: `claude -p "<role prompt>" --permission-mode
   105	    acceptEdits --allowedTools ...` (allowlist per role: reviewers read-only).
   106	  - codex roles: `codex exec -C <root> -s <sandbox> --model <m> -c
   107	    model_reasoning_effort=<e> "<prompt>" </dev/null` (stdin closed — the
   108	    stdin-hang class is a known field failure).
   109	  - Verdict contract: children end with the structured tail
   110	    (`VERDICT: APPROVED|APPROVED_WITH_NOTES|BLOCKED` + FINDINGS) already used
   111	    by every review gate; the supervisor parses exactly that.
   112	
   113	### Child supervision contract (Gate-1 iteration 1, finding 7)
   114	
   115	`children.mjs` owns the full child lifecycle, not just argv assembly:
   116	
   117	- Spawn detached in its OWN process group; stdin closed at spawn (the
   118	  codex-exec stdin-hang class); per-role timeout → SIGTERM to the group, 10 s
   119	  grace, then SIGKILL to the group (no zombie grandchildren; reap verified in
   120	  tests with a child that forks a sleeper).
   121	- Full child output streams to `.handoff/loop/children/<child-id>.log` with a
   122	  byte cap (head preserved, middle truncated with a marker — the verdict tail
   123	  is at the END so the tail is never truncated).
   124	- **Verdict parsing is region-bounded (prompt-echo defense)**: only the
   125	  child's FINAL message region is parsed — claude-code children run with a
   126	  structured output format and the parser reads the result field; codex
   127	  children are parsed strictly AFTER the last `tokens used` marker. The
   128	  prompt region (which quotes `VERDICT:` in its instructions) is never
   129	  scanned. Multiple tails in the final region → the LAST one wins.
   130	- An unparseable, absent, or truncated verdict is BLOCKED-with-escalation,
   131	  never APPROVED; a child that exits after making edits but before a verdict
   132	  parks the subtask with its worktree preserved for inspection.
   133	- A generic nonzero exit classifies as `other-error` (existing classifier
   134	  rule) → the loop retries once, then parks; it NEVER triggers limit failover
   135	  without limit-specific evidence.
   136	- Fixture-driven tests: prompt echo, multiple verdict tails, truncated
   137	  transcript, timeout kill/reap, zombie grandchild, non-limit nonzero exit.
   138	
   139	### Supervisor lifetime and recovery (Gate-1 iteration 2, finding 5)
   140	
   141	"Survives the operator's session ending" is a defined mechanism, not a hope:
   142	
   143	- `baton loop run` is FOREGROUND by default. `--detach` re-launches the
   144	  supervisor in its own session (`setsid`), output to
   145	  `.handoff/loop/supervisor.log`, and returns.
   146	- A run lock `.handoff/loop/supervisor.lock` carries {pid, process
   147	  start-time, host, runId} — the same provably-dead machinery as the
   148	  Layer-1 bundle lock. A second `loop run` against a LIVE supervisor is
   149	  refused; against a provably-dead one it recovers.
   150	- The state machine is journal-replayable: recovery replays
   151	  `journal.ndjson`, marks any in-flight child of the dead supervisor as
   152	  interrupted (its process group is gone or killed on adoption), and either
   153	  continues from the last completed step or parks with an escalation note —
   154	  never re-runs a completed gate iteration.
   155	- Acceptance adds a supervisor-death test: kill the supervisor (and its
   156	  launching session) mid-subtask → a fresh `loop run` recovers via the
   157	  journal and continues or parks; no orphaned children survive (process
   158	  groups reaped on adoption).
   159	
   160	- **Smoke gate (staleness-proof — Gate-1 iteration 1, finding 8; TDD order —
   161	  iteration 2, finding 2)**: after gate-1, the smoke slice is built as a TDD
   162	  mini-cycle (test-author writes the failing smoke assertion → test-verifier
   163	  approves it → implementer writes only enough to pass it — the repo TDD
   164	  contract applies to the slice, not just to subtasks); the supervisor then
   165	  runs `smoke.cmd`, records output, and STOPS, writing
   166	  `.handoff/loop/SMOKE-REVIEW.md` plus `smoke-approval.json` containing an
   167	  approval token = digest over {loop-state digest, smoke.cmd, output digest,
   168	  HEAD, content-sensitive git digest (existing snapshot machinery), child
   169	  assignment}. Resuming requires `baton loop run --approve-smoke <token>`;
   170	  the supervisor recomputes the digest first and REFUSES a drifted token
   171	  (anything changed since the human looked) — it parks for a fresh smoke run
   172	  instead. No full-run budget is spent before a valid approval.
   173	- **Limit failover (the baton integration — Gate-1 iteration 1, finding 3)**:
   174	  an exact transaction, not a loose chain. On child death: (1) reap the
   175	  process group and freeze the transcript; (2) classify via `baton detect`;
   176	  non-limit → the retry/park path above. On a limit classification:
   177	  (3) checkpoint the loop position INTO THE BUNDLE (supervisor
   178	  `checkpoint --session loop-<runId>`) so the seal carries it and the receipt
   179	  token binds it; (4) seal via `finalize --reason-class usage-limit --root
   180	  <mainRoot>` (an already-dead/unsealed bundle takes the degraded-open path
